framework.name: SHAPE America National Standards for K-12 Physical Education
framework.source: https://www.shapeamerica.org/standards/pe (standards 1 to 5; wording is the school's own)

objectives.description: Explain the five components of health-related fitness and give an example of each.
Complete a baseline fitness assessment, including aerobic capacity, strength and flexibility, and record the results.
Set a personal SMART fitness goal and write a plan for reaching it.

strands.strand: Standard 1: Motor Skills and Movement Patterns
strands.subStrand: Standard 1: Motor Skills and Movement Patterns

objectives.description: Perform a dynamic warm-up and cool-down with correct form.
Demonstrate the basic skills of a net game, such as serving and volleying, with control.
Apply simple offensive and defensive tactics in a small-sided game.
Follow safety rules and equipment procedures, and show respect for teammates and officials.
Work with a team to resolve a conflict about the rules of a game.

strands.strand: Standard 1: Motor Skills and Movement Patterns
strands.subStrand: Standard 1: Motor Skills and Movement Patterns

objectives.description: Perform the basic skills of a striking or fielding game.
Take and record resting and exercise heart rate and explain what it shows.
Describe how regular activity benefits physical, mental and social health.
Design and carry out a short circuit workout that uses large muscle groups.
Describe the effects of sleep, nutrition and stress on health and performance.
Analyze the influence of media and peers on health behaviors.
Identify the risks of tobacco, alcohol and vaping and strategies for refusing them.
Explain the rules, scoring and strategy of a team sport in your own words.
Reflect on the activities you enjoy and how you might continue them outside school.
Reassess your fitness at the end of the quarter and compare it with your baseline.
Compare your fitness results with healthy-range standards and identify strengths and goals.
Design a personal fitness plan with a goal, a schedule and measures of progress.
Apply the FITT principle to design a workout for strength or endurance.

strands.strand: Standard 1: Motor Skills and Movement Patterns
strands.subStrand: Standard 1: Motor Skills and Movement Patterns

objectives.description: Demonstrate fundamental movement skills for an invasion game, such as passing, cutting and shooting.
Use offensive and defensive tactics such as spacing and zone defense in a game.
Analyze a game performance using a simple checklist and suggest improvements.
Take on the role of referee or scorekeeper and apply the rules fairly.
Demonstrate sportsmanship in winning, losing and disagreement.

strands.strand: Standard 1: Motor Skills and Movement Patterns
strands.subStrand: Standard 1: Motor Skills and Movement Patterns

objectives.description: Demonstrate basic skills in a lifetime activity, such as badminton, pickleball or yoga.
Measure body composition or fitness using accepted methods and explain what the data shows.
Explain how muscles and the cardiovascular system respond to exercise.
Describe how culture and community shape the games people play.
Explain the components of a balanced diet and read a nutrition label.
Evaluate fitness and nutrition claims in advertising.
Describe strategies for managing stress through activity and relaxation.
Practice basic first aid and describe how to respond to a sports injury.
Choose an activity that challenges you and describe its value for social connection.
Complete a quarter reassessment and reflect on your progress toward your goal.
Review fitness assessment data and write a plan to address a weakness.
Design a strength training program using appropriate exercises, sets and repetitions.
Explain safe lifting technique and spotting.

strands.strand: Standard 1: Motor Skills and Movement Patterns
strands.subStrand: Standard 1: Motor Skills and Movement Patterns

objectives.description: Demonstrate competent skills in at least two lifetime activities, such as tennis, golf or bowling.
Use game strategy such as transition and tempo to gain an advantage.
Analyze video of your own performance and set a specific improvement goal.
Lead a warm-up or small-group activity and give constructive feedback.
Cooperate in a group challenge that requires communication and shared planning.
Explain how aerobic and anaerobic energy systems support different kinds of activity.
Plan a week of training for a 5K run or similar event.
Evaluate community resources for physical activity, such as parks, gyms and clubs.
Analyze barriers to being active and describe ways to overcome them.
Describe how substance use affects performance and long-term health.
Describe the components of healthy relationships and consent.
Explain how to access reliable health information and services.
Describe the signs of stress, anxiety and depression and how to seek help.
Carry out a personal fitness test again and compare with your baseline.
Write a reflection on how physical activity fits into your plans after graduation.
Assess your personal fitness and set an adult-level fitness goal for the year.
Create a fitness plan you can follow after graduation without a gym.
Evaluate a fitness program or product for safety and effectiveness.

strands.strand: Standard 1: Motor Skills and Movement Patterns
strands.subStrand: Standard 1: Motor Skills and Movement Patterns

objectives.description: Demonstrate advanced skills in a chosen activity and teach the basics to a peer.
Plan and run a small tournament, including the rules, schedule and scoring.
Analyze the strategies of a professional or collegiate team in a game.
Serve as a peer leader, setting expectations for safety and fair play.
Resolve a conflict in a group by listening, negotiating and agreeing to a plan.
Design a training plan for a specific goal such as a 5K run, using progression.
Use technology such as heart-rate monitors or apps to monitor activity and interpret the data.
Identify community opportunities for lifelong activity and compare costs and access.
Describe the role of physical activity in managing stress at college or work.
Describe how to prevent and respond to injuries and common emergencies, including CPR.
Analyze how alcohol, drugs and sleep loss affect decision-making and safety.
Make a plan for managing your health care and insurance as an adult.
Describe the influences on healthy eating and plan a week of low-cost meals.
Re-test your fitness at the end of the quarter and compare it with your goals.
Write a personal health and wellness plan for the first year after high school.
